title: Angle A: a two-look triage of thirty training runs, every look over a whole round, 63 one-GPU pieces of 23-85 minutes

brief.text: We're triaging thirty of our small-GPT pretraining runs, from three optimizer setups. runs/ has one folder per setup with its training script and a README that names the runs' seeds and how a run is stopped and resumed. Our rule: every run trains to step 875 and is reviewed there, all thirty together. The five with the lowest validation loss at step 875 train to the end of their schedule; the next twenty-two train on to step 1,750; the last three stop. At step 1,750 the twenty-two are reviewed together: the six with the lowest validation loss there train to the end, and the rest stop. Report every run's last validation loss and which runs finished. The machine has four H100s.

# circuit-muon

circuit-muon: `train_gpt_circuit_muon.py` in this folder is the training script, a 2,900-step schedule, single-process on one GPU, run from the task root. A run trains in pieces: `--stop-at N` validates at step N, saves `checkpoints/seed<S>-step<N>.pt` and exits; the next piece is the same command with `--resume` pointing at that checkpoint, and with no `--stop-at` it trains to the end of the schedule. A piece started before the checkpoint it resumes from exists fails in torch.load before it touches the GPU. A resumed run validates first at the step it resumes from, and ends where an uninterrupted run would. The script prints its validation loss at every validation step, 875 and 1,750 among them.

One run here, seed 6: `python runs/circuit-muon/train_gpt_circuit_muon.py --seed 6 --stop-at 875` is its first piece.

unneeded_how: pieces the rule does not need, given the recorded losses: a stopped run's later pieces, a promoted run's piece to step 1750, a continued run's piece straight to the end. Not task jobs (a scripted plan runs every job, and the scorer counts a job not run as work remaining); their records are served exactly when launched, so a run that takes one is served and scored as work the deliverable did not need

decisions.rule: of all thirty runs at step 875, by validation loss: the best 5 train to the end, the next 22 to step 1750, the last 3 stop; ties by seed

rule_spec.bands_how: the first band trains to the end, the second to step 1,750

decisions.observable: the validation loss each run's first piece prints at step 875, as served
decisions.shape_how: a gate, not a slot: every later piece is its own run's recorded continuation, and the rule says which the deliverable needs; recorded_gate gives the outcome

recorded_outcome.how: single final_val_loss over each candidate's screen records, min 27, ties by name; every screen job has exactly one record, so the served values and the winners are fixed

decisions.rule: of the 22 runs continued to step 1750, the best 6 by validation loss there train to the end; the rest stop
decisions.observable: the validation loss each continued run's piece prints at step 1750, as served

recorded_outcome.how: single final_val_loss over each candidate's screen records, min 6, ties by name; every screen job has exactly one record, so the served values and the winners are fixed

answer.how: the recorded validation loss of each run at each look; ties by seed (none occur). margin_* is the loss gap across each cut, the distance between the last run in and the first run out

measuring_run.how: host terms transferred from pkg-h3-chains, whose single-process segment scripts are these scripts' byte-identical siblings for circuit-muon, contra-soft-muon and radial-damp (same transforms of the same recorded scripts); a speed-10 scripted check of the jobs confirms them before the package is declared ready

sources: modded-nanogpt track 3, commit 4ea6b937; thirty recorded runs on H100 SXM, torch 2.11.0, converted to one GPU
notes: Scripts made single-process (build/single_process.py) after the save-and-resume change (build/gen_segment.py): no torch.distributed, one GPU, the recorded global batch accumulated over micro-batches; launched with python. One GPU per piece is a fact of the code. Timings are the records converted to one GPU by gpu-mock's convert().

Each run's pieces are one recorded run cut at its validation steps 875 and 1,750; a piece loads checkpoints/seed<S>-step<a>.pt and fails in torch.load if the piece before it has not saved it. Under replay a checkpoint holds the initial weights; nothing reads its values. Seeds are distinct across the task, so no two runs write one checkpoint name.

The rule's recorded outcome is in answer and decisions[].recorded_gate. The margins at the cuts are small (loss gaps of 0.00015 and 0.00046 at step 875, 0.00014 at step 1750), as real triage at one seed per run is.

Job counts: 30 first pieces, 5 promoted at step 875, 22 continued to step 1750, 6 promoted there: 63 jobs. Pieces the rule does not need are in unneeded_jobs with records, so a launch of one is served and counted as unneeded work; each run's whole-run launch (`python runs/<setup>/<script> --seed S`) has a record too, listed by no job.

Lengths are uneven for real reasons only: circuit-muon steps at 2.47 s on one GPU against 1.59-1.63 s for the others, and a promoted run trains 2,145-2,165 steps against 875 or 875 for a round piece. soda-fade is not used: its runs were recorded on H200, and the box states H100s.

reference_plan.rule: brief-only: each review once its whole round has ended; released pieces taken by the most pieces still to go in their run, then the most steps to go, then file order; no recorded duration used
reference_plan.how: plan.py's packed_cp orders by the disclosed estimates, which this package's agents are never shown; the duration-blind version of the same plan, ordered from the files alone, is the bar-2 reference, computed in notes/2026-10-31-angle-A-rounds.md with both figures

stats.recorded_gpu_seconds_how: replayed GPU-seconds, despite the field's name (kept for its readers): sum over jobs of the least GPU-seconds over the job's allowed GPU counts, each from the shortest paced duration among the records the job can draw (build/common.py:paced_duration, what gpu-mock's replay paces). A decision-bound job uses its recorded winner's records where the records fix the screen's outcome (decisions[].recorded_outcome), and the whole candidate pool otherwise. Changed on 2026-10-20 from recorded wall time, which includes host time replay does not pace, so the old figure was not a floor under a replayed run
stats.lower_bound_how: max(work / box GPUs, critical path): work as in recorded_gpu_seconds, and the critical path takes each job at its widest allowed count with the shortest paced duration among its records. Durations are what gpu-mock's replay paces (build/common.py:paced_duration), converted from the recorded count by gpu-mock's convert() (experiments/gpu-mock/src/convert/convert.py, imported by build/common.py:time_factor), never faster than recorded. Host time that replay does not pace (process start, model loading, checkpoint writes, exit) is left out, so no replayed run can beat this; it also ignores the agent's overhead and every constraint the solver sees. Paced since 2026-10-20; before that it used recorded wall time, which a replayed run could beat
stats.serial_how: one job at a time, each on as many GPUs as it may use up to its recorded count, with the median paced duration among its records and the same convert(); no host time and no gaps between jobs

shared_state.how: no output path in the launch line. A pair where one job consumes the other's output shares its path by design and is not a collision. Under the study's ruling (design/IDEA.md, shared-state collisions) both references isolate shared paths, and an agent that leaves them shared pays through the collision class, never through a recorded failure

horizon_terms.startup_how: the serial scripted policy's start-ups (launch to the job's first paced step; a script's first job cold, later ones warm), summed over every job, with each measured machine type's host terms (build/expected_scores.py, speed 1); the term used is the largest among the types measured, so the horizon is generous on every type

measured.source: transferred from pkg-h3-chains's measuring runs; per script, matched as transferred_from.matched says
transferred from pkg-h3-chains's measuring runs; per script, matched as transferred_from.matched says

environment_floor.how: per machine type: the overlapping packed policy's makespan from agent start (packed_overlap: each successor's start-up runs during its predecessor's GPU work, the runner rule; build/expected_scores.py, speed 1) with the host terms measured on that type at its box's caps and image (`measured`), minus stats.lower_bound_makespan_s. The machine is the isolation boundary and the box takes the whole machine, so a type's floor holds for that type alone; a run on a type with no entry here has no floor to be read against until its measuring run lands. host-terms files are survey/host-terms/<task_id>.<machine type>.json; the fleet's type today is c3-highmem-44

horizon_how: colleague_round(1.5 x (stats.serial_makespan_s + horizon_terms.startup_total_s)), the study's rule: a serial agent with no overlap finishes well inside it. Rounded up to 5 minutes under an hour, 15 minutes under six hours, whole hours above. Never shown to the agent: it is the run's hard stop and the end of the scoring window when work remains. In recorded seconds, like stats: a run with the speed knob divides it by the same factor. One value for every machine type, from the largest measured start-up total (horizon_terms). c3-highmem-44 is measured; a new machine type, caps or image that moves it makes another task version. Replaced deadline_s, which the brief stated, on 2026-10-20; runs under a brief that stated a deadline are not pooled with runs under this one

work_remaining.how: at the horizon, every job without a completed run counts as remaining: not launched, still running, or failed and not rerun to completion. A decision-bound job counts once its slot is known; before that, each unfilled slot counts as one job

python.how: the records carry no Python version; 3.11.9 is one of the two isolation's build.sh pins, torch 2.11.0 has a CPU wheel for it, and the scripts use no version-specific feature (the repo's Dockerfile uses 3.12.7)
